repo_notes.content: DomainForge is the canonical Rust semantic compiler and projection engine for the .sea Semantic Executable Abstraction DSL, not simply a code generator. Trace .sea → Pest grammar/AST → module resolution/semantic graph → validation/governance → operator-family projection → emitted artifacts and independent validation. The source model is canonical; projections do not become alternative sources of domain truth. Prioritize domainforge-core/ and execution evidence over marketing copy.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Instruction scope is essential: root AGENTS.md governs all; domainforge-core/AGENTS.md governs Rust/compiler/bindings; .agents/AGENTS.md governs state, evidence and handoffs. Read .agents/current_state.md and next_steps.md as current but possibly branch-specific observations. Source code and tests outrank stale historical notes. Do not duplicate root agents instructions in wiki.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Grammar and schema evolution is gated. domainforge-core/grammar/sea.pest, parser AST/conversion, semantic graph and all affected projections/bindings must move together. The project checks for an ADR for SEA language changes via scripts/check-sea-language-change.sh. Preserve existing namespace rules, content-addressed ConceptId, IndexMap order, rust_decimal quantities, units and three-valued policy evaluation. Link the correct ADR/PRD/SDS to each topic.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Projections use the operator family pattern (ADR-011), typed target IRs, deterministic IDs and ArtifactSink containment. A generated schema or policy is not runtime execution, enforcement or externally validated settlement. Distinguish exact projection family, supported subset, refusals, fidelity-report class, native ecosystem tool checks and remaining obligations. Generated pkg/, dist/, native .node and wheel artifacts are build outputs, not sources to hand-edit.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: The .sea application contract and canonical semantic envelope model operational boundaries, typed records/enums/operations, authority fact resolution, policy decisions, source hashes, identity and approval semantics. Do not infer that generating application contracts starts an HTTP server or grants real authority. Governance, payment and evidence gates must be described separately from generated representations.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: DomainForge includes Rego/OPA and OpenShell projections in the current main source (domainforge-core/src/projection/rego and openshell). Rego emits a constrained decision bundle and is differential-tested against OPA 1.21.1; it does not execute OPA or enforce policy. OpenShell projects the shared Cell IR to policy.yaml and sandbox/mapping/lock contracts for OpenShell v0.1.3; it does not start a sandbox or prove runtime isolation. Unsupported semantics are rejected; both PROOFS.md claims are partial. Do not extrapolate to every Rego/OpenShell feature.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Cell projection is governed infrastructure intent, not a container runtime: CellIr under projection/cell, environment declarations, resources/network, mount mappings, profiles, typed refusals, receipts/locks and evidence obligations. Compare cell vs devbox/mise vs openshell projectors and emphasize shared IR, trust boundaries, deterministic outputs and executor settlement requirements.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Rust core is authoritative. Python binds via PyO3/maturin (domainforge-python and core/src/python), TypeScript via napi-rs and Bun (domainforge-typescript and core/src/typescript), WASM via wasm-bindgen (core/src/wasm). Public primitive changes require cross-binding tests; default WASM intentionally excludes CLI-only projection families because of bundle size. Never claim Rust-only green proves foreign language parity.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Use justfile as the primary command contract: just rust-test, python-test, ts-test, all-tests, enterprise-verify, prove, cell-verify, rego-verify and openshell-verify. PROOFS.md records proven/partial/planned/blocked claims with exact scripts and independent validators. The live CI is a large multijob matrix including Rust/Linux/macOS/Windows, MSRV, Python, TypeScript, WASM, security and projection toolchains; a documentation-only PR should still await required checks rather than assume success.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Toolchain details: rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.99.0; domainforge-core Cargo.toml states MSRV 1.89; CI tests both. Bun is preferred for TypeScript despite Node 24 setup in CI; Python distribution requires Python >=3.11 and maturin. Root devbox.json and justfile are available but making Nix/Devbox or full native ecosystem proof tools mandatory for Devin snapshots is unnecessary and expensive. Never install secrets/signing keys or run deployment during a basic snapshot.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Provenance and freshness matter: .agents/current_state.md can contain historical branch-specific claims (e.g. 'not merged' while files already exist on main); check main branch paths and commits before reporting current status. Don't treat previous console outputs, docs, or checked boxes as freshly executed tests. DeepWiki is a navigational representation, not a new source of implementation truth.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers

repo_notes.content: Related repos domainforge-lsp and domainforge-vsc-extension are independent repositories and not part of this repo's Rust workspace. Describe in-repo CLI/FFI surfaces and external editor integration boundaries without pretending their separate code is present here. The .sea registry and semantic packs model namespace/closure/fingerprints; use code and tests for exact behavior.
repo_notes.author: DomainForge maintainers
